newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent seen up 5-10 cts, gas oil up $1-$1.50.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent seen up 5-10 cts, gas oil up $1-$1.50.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures were expected to open firmer on Monday, encouraged by refinery problems which were keeping Atlantic basin gasoline prices strong, dealers said.
"The market has its own fundamental strength at the moment coming mainly from gasoline as cracker by cracker goes down," said a broker.

Sept Brent settled at $18.95 a barrel on Friday but was expected to open in London 5-10 cents firmer in line with modest gains in Singapore. Aug gas oil, which closed at $171.50 a tonne, was expected to open $1-$1.50 firmer.
Both contracts ended steady on Friday after early losses were reversed on news of technical problems at three gasoline production units in northwest Europe.

Dealers expected a cautious extension of the bullish sentiment in early Monday dealing but said most of the market would be watching the United Nations for any signs of progress towards a resumption of limited Iraqi oil exports.
"The U.N. is still the key to the entire market," said one.
A U.N. spokesman said on Thursday approval of Iraq's aid plan, the last major obstacle to renewed exports, should be completed early this week.
"Each day that goes by without approval adds another 10 cents or so to the upside," said a broker.
Approval of the aid plan could be followed by renewed exports of Iraqi crude in little more than a week, exerting immediate pressure on spot markets.
But the reaction on Brent futures could be more muted.
"We've seen early selling in London in the last few sessions as people take on short positions in anticipation of the news. That could limit the downside," said a broker.
Sept Brent was expected to run into resistance around $19.08-$19.10 a barrel. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
